items.difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X -> Y of quasi-separated and quasi-compact schemes, and L in D_QCoh(O_X), K in D_QCoh(O_Y), the lemma asserts that the map of equation labelled equation-sheafy-trace induces an isomorphism RHom_X(L, a(K)) -> RHom_Y(Rf_*L, K) of global derived Homs (statement lines 877-907). By the construction of global RHom in Cohomology, Section labelled cohomology-section-global-RHom one has RHom_X(L, a(K)) = RGamma(X, RSheafHom(L, a(K))) = RGamma(Y, Rf_*RSheafHom(L, a(K))) and RHom_Y(Rf_*L, K) = RGamma(Y, RSheafHom(Rf_*L, K)), so the lemma reduces to Lemma labelled lemma-iso-on-RSheafHom (proof lines 909-922). The proof concludes that a map E -> E' in D(O_Y) inducing an isomorphism DQ_Y(E) -> DQ_Y(E') induces a quasi-isomorphism RGamma(Y, E) -> RGamma(Y, E'): indeed H^i(Y, E) = Ext^i_Y(O_Y, E) = Hom(O_Y[-i], E) = Hom(O_Y[-i], DQ_Y(E)) because O_Y[-i] is quasi-coherent and DQ_Y is the right adjoint to the inclusion (proof lines 922-931). Reducing the global statement to the sheaf level and then reading it off the coherator adjunction is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
